text: The Studienstiftung is a German scholarship foundation established in 1948, originally as a department of the Deutsche Studentenschaft, which was dissolved under National Socialism and re-founded in Cologne. It provides financial and academic support to undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral students, with eligibility based on BAFöG criteria and full-time study requirements. Students are nominated through various channels including schools, universities, examination boards, competitions, and self-identification via an assessment test. Scholarships include a monthly allowance, need-based subsidies, and support for health insurance, with additional funding available for students with children. Academic support includes summer schools, research groups, language courses, and mentoring. The foundation offers internal programs like the KAUST-Studienstiftung and the Beethoven House residence scholarships, as well as open programs such as the McCloy, ERP, and Carlo-Schmid programs. As of 2023, the foundation approved 2,179 undergraduate and 301 doctoral scholarships. Statistics show that the proportion of Studienstiftung scholars among university students in Germany has remained stable around 0.48% from 2013 to 2023. Notable alumni include Nobel laureates, Fields Medalists, and prominent figures in science, politics, and the arts.
